_comment: QR ids for cards we hold under a serial-style id. Our numeric ids ARE the QR id already, so only serial-style cards need this. The number is what the publisher's own card page is keyed by: obsidianprotocol.net/#/info?id=<qr>&lang=en, which is what the QR code on the card opens.
_source: The QR ID column of the championship parts lists (2026-08-03), then EVERY pair verified against the live API by name on 2026-08-10. Nothing here is taken on trust from the spreadsheet alone. Extended 2026-08-10 by walking the API id space 1-600 and matching each record's title back to a card name, which is the only route for pilots: their sheet QR column restarts at 1 per sheet and the UN pilot sheet has no QR values at all.
_trap: A pilot's id is NOT the number printed in the parts list's QR ID column, and reading it straight resolves to the wrong card entirely: the six RDL pilots carry QR 1-6, and API ids 1-6 are backpacks and armaments, so FPA-01 'Misty' would resolve to the SH-15 Field Repair System. Always confirm against the name the API returns before adding an entry here.
_offset: CORRECTED 2026-08-11. The cause is not what this file said before ('the column restarts per sheet type', which was inferred from the RDL sheet alone and does not survive contact with the others). The pilot block in the API begins at 300, and the RDL and UN sheets print the pilot's INDEX inside that block while the PD sheet prints the full id. So: API id = sheet QR + 300 for RDL and UN, and = sheet QR for PD. Verified exhaustively - all 12 RDL and UN pilots we hold come out at exactly +300 with no exceptions (Misty 1->301 ... Sealock 24->324), and PD's 369/370 match the API by name with no offset at all. Two consequences: the UN sheet is NOT empty as previously recorded, it prints 19-24; and the sheet IS usable for pilots once the rule is applied, rather than being unusable as the old note claimed. It still is not a substitute for the name check, because the two KeyHole pilots share a name and the sheet lists one under each convention (6 and 362).
_ambiguity: Name matching is only sound where the name is unique, and two names are not. The two KeyHole pilots reach us identically named, so id 306 matched both; the API separates them as 'KeyHole' (306) and 'Keyhole - Hidden in Plain Sight' (362), and OTTO scanned 362 off the RDL Dune card, which leaves 306 for the Cavalry pilot. The other clash is S100 Shield + R6SS SMG (D): our S100+R6SS-L-T is the LEFT hand and card 116 the RIGHT, sharing one name, so the serial card is deliberately still unlinked rather than risk pointing at its mirror. Every other pair was cross-checked on points - 25 of 25 agreed.
